Control Chart for Instrument Drift

Source: R/control_chart.R
control_chart.Rd

Builds a control chart of a quantity that should stay constant over time, such as the intensity of an internal standard line, a line ratio of a check sample or a plasma temperature, to detect drifts and shifts of the instrument: a Shewhart chart of individual values, an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) or a cumulative sum (CUSUM).

Usage

control_chart(
  x,
  order = NULL,
  method = "shewhart",
  baseline = NULL,
  center = NULL,
  sigma = NULL,
  width = 3,
  rules = TRUE,
  lambda = 0.2,
  allowance = 0.5,
  decision = 5
)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector of the monitored quantity.

order

The time or acquisition order of the values (numbers, dates or date-times), by which they are sorted. By default, their position.

method

"shewhart" (default), "ewma" or "cusum".

baseline

The measurements that set the center and the standard deviation: the number of first values, or a logical or index vector. By default, all values.

center, sigma

The center and standard deviation of the process, if known.

width

The width of the limits, in standard deviations, for the Shewhart and EWMA charts. Default is 3.

rules

A logical: apply the Western Electric rules to the Shewhart chart (TRUE, default).

lambda

The smoothing constant of the EWMA chart. Default is 0.2.

allowance, decision

The allowance \(k\) and decision interval \(h\) of the CUSUM chart, in standard deviations. Default is 0.5 and 5.

Value

A tibble of class specproc_control_chart, one row per value in time order: order, value, the plotted statistic (the value, the EWMA, or for the CUSUM the upper sum, with the lower sum in lower_sum), the center, the lower and upper limits, whether the point is a signal, and, for the Shewhart chart, the first Western Electric rule broken. The method, center, standard deviation and baseline are in the attributes. Draw it with plot_control_chart().

Details

The center line and the standard deviation \(\sigma\) are estimated from the baseline measurements (by default, all of them), unless given: the mean, and the mean moving range of consecutive values divided by 1.128, which, unlike the standard deviation, is little inflated by a drift.

  • "shewhart": the values themselves, with limits at width \(\sigma\) from the center. With rules = TRUE, the Western Electric rules also flag (1) a value beyond the limits, (2) two of three consecutive values beyond \(2\sigma\) on the same side, (3) four of five beyond \(1\sigma\) on the same side and (4) eight consecutive values on the same side of the center. It detects large shifts quickly.

  • "ewma": \(z_t = \lambda x_t + (1 - \lambda) z_{t-1}\), starting at the center, with limits at width \(\sigma \sqrt{\lambda / (2 - \lambda) (1 - (1 - \lambda)^{2t})}\). Small values of \(\lambda\) detect small, slow drifts.

  • "cusum": the tabular CUSUM, the sums of the deviations beyond allowance \(\sigma\) above and below the center, \(C^+_t = \max(0, x_t - \mu - k\sigma + C^+_{t-1})\) and likewise below, with a signal when a sum exceeds decision \(\sigma\). It detects small persistent shifts.

References

  • Montgomery, D.C. (2019). Introduction to Statistical Quality Control, 8th ed. Wiley, Hoboken.

  • Western Electric Company (1956). Statistical Quality Control Handbook. Western Electric, Indianapolis.

See also

plot_control_chart(), line_intensities()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

# a check-sample ratio that drifts after the 60th measurement
set.seed(1)
ratio <- 1 + c(rep(0, 60), seq(0, 0.06, length.out = 40)) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.02)
shewhart <- control_chart(ratio, baseline = 40)
shewhart[shewhart$signal, ]

# the EWMA detects the slow drift earlier
plot_control_chart(control_chart(ratio, method = "ewma", baseline = 40))
